en: to be time-worn; to be decrepit

examples.en: This building has become very worn out.
We need to replace the aged water pipes.

examples.ko: 우리 아파트는 너무 노후해서 비가 새요.
examples.en: Our apartment is so old that it leaks when it rains.
If school facilities are worn out, safety is a concern.

examples.ko: 노후하다는 이유로 다리를 새로 짓기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided to rebuild the bridge because it is aging.

examples.ko: 노후한 기계 때문에 공장이 자주 멈춰요.
examples.en: The factory often stops because of its worn-out machines.

explain: '노후하다'는 건물, 다리, 기계처럼 오래 써서 낡고 약해졌다는 뜻이에요. 물건이나 시설에만 쓰고 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 사람이 나이 들 때는 '늙다'를 쓰고, 일반 물건이 낡을 때는 '낡다'가 훨씬 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: They are renovating the aging facilities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양이에요. 건물이나 시설이 오래돼서 약해졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, used for buildings or facilities that have become old and weak.

phrases.en: The bridge is old and worn, so it is dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡은 것이 이유가 되어 다음 말이 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when being worn out is the reason for what follows.

phrases.en: This building is not worn out yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 낡지 않았다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that something is not yet worn out.

explain_en: 노후하다 is only for things such as buildings, bridges and machines that have grown old and weak through long use, never for people. For people, use 늙다. For ordinary worn items, 낡다 is much more common.

en: to be damp; to be moist

examples.en: The snack has absorbed moisture and gone soggy.

examples.ko: 장마철에는 이불이 눅눅해서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: In the rainy season the blanket feels damp and I can't sleep.
I don't want to eat soggy seaweed.

examples.ko: 빨래가 눅눅하게 덜 말라서 다시 돌렸어요.
examples.en: The laundry didn't dry fully and stayed damp, so I ran it again.
Eat the fried food quickly before it gets soggy.
If the room feels damp, try turning on a dehumidifier.

explain: '습하다'는 공기나 날씨가 습할 때 쓰고, '눅눅하다'는 과자, 옷, 이불처럼 바삭하거나 보송해야 할 것이 물기를 먹어 축축할 때 써요. 반대로는 '바삭하다'나 '보송보송하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Because of the rain, the blanket feels damp.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눅눅한'으로 물기를 먹은 물건을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '눅눅한' describes things that have absorbed moisture.

phrases.en: If you leave the snack bag open, it gets soggy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바삭하던 것이 물기를 먹어 변하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something crisp becoming moist.

phrases.en: This seaweed isn't soggy, it's crispy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 바삭하거나 보송하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, it means the thing is crisp or dry.

explain_en: '습하다' is for humid air or weather, while '눅눅하다' is for things like snacks, clothes or blankets that should be crisp or dry but have taken on moisture. The opposites are '바삭하다' (crispy) and '보송보송하다' (dry and fluffy).

en: to be small; to be simple

examples.en: My family is small because there are few members.
The newlyweds' home had little furniture, so it was simple.
I want to have a small, simple wedding.
My belongings were few, so the move ended quickly.
The table setting is simple, but the taste is really good.
For this trip, I packed my bag light.

explain: 식구, 살림, 짐, 상차림처럼 사람이나 물건의 수가 적고 군더더기가 없을 때 써요. '간단하다'가 복잡하지 않다는 느낌이라면, 단출하다는 가짓수가 적어서 깔끔한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The newlyweds' simple household looks neat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가진 물건이 적고 간단한 살림을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a household with few belongings.

phrases.en: We are a small family of just three.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식구가 적은 가족을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a family with few members.

phrases.en: I set a simple birthday table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 준비를 적게 하되 깔끔하게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preparing only a few things, but neatly.

explain_en: Use it when the number of people or things is small and there is nothing extra, such as family members, belongings, luggage or a meal. While '간단하다' feels uncomplicated, 단출하다 feels neat because there are few items.

examples.en: The wooden floor was cold, so I put on socks.
The child lay down on the wooden floor and fell asleep.
I wiped the wooden floor clean with a rag.
The old wooden floor creaks.

examples.ko: 집 안 마룻바닥은 나무로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The floor inside the house is made of wood.
I laid a blanket on the wooden floor and slept.

explain: 그냥 '바닥'보다 나무판을 깐 마루의 바닥이라는 느낌이 있어요. 사이시옷이 있어서 '마루빠닥'처럼 소리 나요. 아파트 거실처럼 나무 바닥에는 '마루'나 '마룻바닥'을 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 집 거실은 마루가 깔려 있어요.
phrases.en: The living room in our house has a wood floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마룻바닥'보다 짧게, 나무판을 깐 곳 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter word for the wooden-floored area itself.

phrases.en: There was no chair, so I sat on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 어디에 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the particle '에' to say where someone is or does something.
phrases.en_equiv: to sit on the wooden floor

phrases.en: I wipe the wooden floor every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about cleaning.

explain_en: Compared with plain '바닥', it suggests the floor of a '마루' laid with wooden boards. Because of the 사이시옷, it is pronounced like '마루빠닥'. For wooden floors such as an apartment living room, '마루' or '마룻바닥' is used.

en: to be separated; to be divided

examples.en: Trash is separated by type.
The lid comes off easily.
The two rooms were divided by a wall.
When work and home are separate, my mind is at ease.
Please put the detached part back on.
It's a machine that can't be detached from the body.

explain: '분리되다'는 붙어 있던 것이 떨어질 때 써요. 내가 떼어 놓으면 '분리하다'예요. 쓰레기는 '분리수거'라고 해서 종류별로 나눠 버리는 일을 말해요.

phrases.en: I sort the recycling on Sundays.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰레기를 종류별로 나눠 버리는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sorting trash by type for disposal.

phrases.en: I separate the bottle and the lid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 떼어 놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person does the separating.

phrases.en: This part does not come apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙은 것이 떨어지지 않는다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning attached parts don't come off.

explain_en: 분리되다 is used when something that was attached comes apart. If you detach it yourself it is 분리하다. For trash, 분리수거 means sorting waste by type for disposal.

examples.en: I saw stone tools from the Paleolithic age at the museum.
I heard people long ago hunted animals with stone tools.

examples.ko: 이 유적에서 오래된 석기가 많이 발견됐어요.
examples.en: Many old stone tools were found at this site.
People did not use metal in the Stone Age.
The archaeologist took a piece of a stone tool out of the ground.

examples.ko: 석기는 날카로워서 칼처럼 쓸 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Stone tools were sharp, so they could be used like knives.

explain: '구석기', '신석기'처럼 역사 수업과 박물관 이야기에서 나오고, '청동기', '철기'로 이어지는 역사 용어예요. '석기'는 사람 이름으로도 쓰이니까 문맥으로 구분해요.

phrases.en: People in the Stone Age lived in caves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌로 도구를 만들던 옛날 시대를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the ancient era when tools were made of stone.

phrases.en: In the Neolithic era, people began farming.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구석기 시대' 다음에 오는 시대예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The era that comes after the 구석기 (Paleolithic) era.

phrases.example: 옛날 사람들은 돌을 깨서 석기를 만들었어요.
phrases.en: People long ago broke stones to make stone tools.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌로 도구를 만드는 일을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe making tools out of stone.

explain_en: It appears in history class and museum talk, as in '구석기' (Paleolithic) and '신석기' (Neolithic), and it leads on to '청동기' (Bronze Age) and '철기' (Iron Age). '석기' is also used as a personal name, so tell them apart by context.

examples.ko: 낚시 갈 때 아이스박스에 음료수를 가득 넣었어요.
examples.en: When we went fishing, I filled the cooler with drinks.

examples.ko: 아이스박스 안에 얼음이 아직 남아 있어요.
examples.en: There is still some ice left in the cooler.
We brought a big cooler to the campsite.
I bought fish and brought it back in a cooler.

examples.ko: 이 아이스박스는 무거워서 혼자 들기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This cooler is heavy, so it's hard to lift alone.

examples.ko: 아이스박스가 없으면 고기가 상할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Without a cooler, the meat could spoil.

explain: 한국어에서는 얼음을 넣어 음식과 음료를 차갑게 들고 다니는 상자만 가리켜요. 집에서 쓰는 냉장고는 '냉장고'라고 해요. 캠핑, 낚시, 소풍 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I packed a cooler for the picnic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나들이 준비를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when preparing for an outing.

phrases.en: I put the fish in the cooler.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 차갑게 보관할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when keeping food cold.

phrases.en: There are drinks inside the cooler.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안에 든 물건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to talk about what is inside.

explain_en: In Korean this only means the portable box you fill with ice to keep food and drinks cold. The fridge at home is just '냉장고'. It often comes up when talking about camping, fishing and picnics.

en: to be comfortable; to be carefree

examples.en: This chair is really comfortable when you sit in it.
I want to rest well in a cozy home.
The hotel room was more comfortable than I expected.
Grandmother is enjoying a comfortable retirement.

examples.ko: 안락하다고 해서 꼭 행복한 것은 아니에요.
examples.en: Being comfortable does not always mean being happy.
If the plane seat is comfortable, a long flight is fine too.

explain: '편안하다'는 몸과 마음이 편한 느낌 전체에 쓰고, '안락하다'는 집, 의자, 생활처럼 환경이 편하고 걱정 없이 지낼 만하다는 쪽이에요. 조금 격식 있는 말이라 일상에서는 '편해요'를 더 많이 써요. '안락한 생활', '안락한 의자'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 안락한 생활을 하고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: He wants to live a comfortable life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정 없이 편하게 지내는 삶을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a life lived at ease without worries.

phrases.en: This sofa isn't very comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 환경이 불편하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, it means the setting is uncomfortable.

phrases.en: I sat in a comfortable chair and read a book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의자나 집처럼 편하게 쉴 수 있는 곳 앞에 '안락한'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 안락한 before a place or object where you can rest comfortably, like a chair or house.

explain_en: '편안하다' covers any feeling of ease in body and mind, while '안락하다' is about a setting such as a home, a chair or a lifestyle that is comfortable and free of worry. It sounds a little formal, so '편해요' is more common in daily talk. Typical uses are '안락한 생활' and '안락한 의자'.

en: to be clean and hygienic; to be well kept

examples.ko: 이 식당은 주방이 늘 청결해서 믿음이 가요.
examples.en: This restaurant's kitchen is always clean, so I trust it.
The habit of washing your hands thoroughly is important.
A hospital needs a clean environment above all else.

examples.ko: 화장실이 청결하지 않으면 손님이 다시 안 와요.
examples.en: If the restroom is not clean, customers will not come back.
The hotel room is much cleaner than I expected.
The shop is known for being clean, so it has many customers.

explain: '깨끗하다'보다 딱딱하고, 위생과 관리 상태가 좋다는 느낌이 강해요. 식당, 병원, 숙소를 평가할 때 자주 나오고 반대말은 '불결하다'예요.

phrases.en: This hotel room is very clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 활용으로 장소가 깨끗하게 관리된다고 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, used to evaluate that a place is kept clean.

phrases.en: The kitchen must always be kept clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위생 상태를 계속 좋게 지킨다는 뜻의 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation meaning to keep hygiene at a good level.

phrases.en: The restroom wasn't clean, so it was uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 불만을 말할 때 쓰고, 더 강하게는 '불결해요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for complaints; '불결해요' is stronger.

explain_en: It is stiffer than '깨끗하다' and stresses good hygiene and upkeep. It often appears when reviewing restaurants, hospitals, and lodgings, and its opposite is '불결하다'.

examples.en: I add just a little bleach to white laundry.

examples.ko: 표백제를 쓸 때는 창문을 열어 주세요.
examples.en: Please open the windows when you use bleach.

examples.ko: 이 표백제는 색깔 있는 옷에 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not use this bleach on colored clothes.
It is dangerous to mix bleach with other detergents.
I wiped the bathroom mold clean with bleach.

examples.ko: 표백제 냄새가 너무 독해서 머리가 아파요.
examples.en: The bleach smell is so strong that I get a headache.

explain: 옷을 희게 하거나 얼룩, 곰팡이를 없애는 약품이에요. 집에서는 염소계 표백제를 흔히 '락스'라고 불러요. '표백제'는 포장이나 설명서에 쓰인 말에 가까워요. 옷에는 '산소계 표백제'처럼 종류를 붙여 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I clean bathroom mold with bleach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서는 표백제보다 '락스'라고 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: At home people say 락스 more often than 표백제.

phrases.example: 색깔 있는 옷에는 산소계 표백제를 써요.
phrases.en: I use oxygen bleach on colored clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷에 쓰는 순한 종류를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A milder type used on clothes.

phrases.en: I mixed bleach into water and washed the rag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물에 섞을 때 '풀다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 풀다 is used for dissolving something in water.

explain_en: It is a chemical that whitens clothes or removes stains and mold. At home, chlorine bleach is commonly called '락스'. '표백제' sounds closer to the wording on labels and instructions. Types are named too, as in '산소계 표백제' (oxygen-based bleach).
